note: Reader notes on the recorded Latin itself. kind: bracket = poetry or section brackets kept from the source edition; spacing = glued initial or stray space; coverage = Latin missing, truncated or repeated on the card; suspected-typo = a word the reader believed misspelt. recorded_latin_words_equal_reference says whether the recorded Latin has the same words as the reference Clementine transcription (mborders/vulgata, from VulSearch); the comparison ignores punctuation, spacing, brackets and markers, so it is not meaningful for the bracket and spacing kinds. Where true, a suspected typo is in that transcription too (or is not a typo) and was not introduced by the site.

notes.latin: pœnituit eum quod hominum fecisset in terra. Et tactus dolore cordis intrinsecus,
notes.english: He regretted having made human beings upon the earth, and, touched with grief deep within His heart,
notes.reason: "quod hominum fecisset" is ungrammatical (genitive plural with no governing noun); the Clementine reads "pœnituit eum quod hominem fecisset in terra". The English already renders the correct sense.

notes.latin: Dixitque de Sara uxore suo : Soror mea est. Misit ergo Abimelech rex Geraræ, et tulit eam.
notes.english: He said of his wife Sarah, “She is my sister.” So Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took her.
notes.reason: "de Sara uxore suo" has the wrong gender; the Clementine reads "Dixitque de Sara uxore sua : Soror mea est." English unaffected.

notes.latin: Si non intercessisset dilatio, jam vice alter venissemus.
notes.english: If there had been no delay, we could have returned a second time by now.”
notes.reason: Latin reads "jam vice alter venissemus"; "alter" cannot agree with feminine ablative "vice". Clementine reads "jam vice altera venissemus" (a second time). The English already renders the correct reading.

notes.latin: Quo cum pervenisset, juncto Joseph curro suo, ascendit obviam patri suo ad eumdem locum : vidensque eum, irruit super collum ejus, et inter amplexus flevit.
notes.english: When he arrived there, Joseph harnessed his chariot and went up to meet his father in that same place. Seeing him, he fell upon his neck and wept as he embraced him.
notes.reason: Latin reads "juncto Joseph curro suo"; "currus" is fourth declension and the Clementine has "juncto Joseph curru suo" (his chariot being harnessed). The English is unaffected.

notes.latin: [Congregamini, et audite, filii Jacob, audite Israël patrem vestrum :
notes.english: Gather and hear, sons of Jacob; hear Israel your father.
notes.reason: Latin begins with a stray opening bracket, "[Congregamini" (source edition's verse-section markup, closed at 49:27). Corrected Latin: "Congregamini, et audite, filii Jacob, audite Israël patrem vestrum :"

notes.latin: Benjamin lupus rapax, mane comedat prædam, et vespere dividet spolia.]
notes.english: Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning let him eat prey, and in the evening he shall divide the spoil.”
notes.reason: Latin ends with a stray closing bracket, "spolia.]" (verse-section markup opened at 49:2). Corrected Latin: "Benjamin lupus rapax, mane comedat prædam, et vespere dividet spolia."

notes.latin: contra Mambre in terra Chanaan, quam emit Abraham cum agro ab Ephron Hethæo in possessionem sepulchri.
notes.english: opposite Mamre in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a possession for burial.
notes.reason: Duplicated verse: this row repeats Vg 49:30 ("contra Mambre in terra Chanaan, quam emit Abraham...") already shown in full at 49:30 (#52); the Vulgate has no separate text for this site verse.

notes.latin: Hæc autem erunt vestimenta quæ faciet : rationale et superhumerale, tunicam et lineam strictam, cidarim et balteum. Facient vestimenta sancta fratri tuo Aaron et filiis ejus, ut sacerdotio fungantur mihi.
notes.english: These are the garments they shall make: a breastpiece and ephod, a robe and fitted linen tunic, a turban and sash. They shall make holy garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, to serve Me as priests.
notes.reason: "vestimenta quæ faciet" appears to be a slip for "quæ facient" (plural, the wise-hearted of v.3; next sentence 'Facient vestimenta sancta'). English 'they shall make' matches facient. Verify against the Clementine.

notes.latin: Ipsum autem arietem secabis in frustra : lotaque intestina ejus ac pedes, pones super concisas carnes, et super caput illius.
notes.english: Cut the ram itself into pieces. Wash its entrails and feet, and place them upon the cut-up flesh and its head.
notes.reason: "secabis in frustra" (frustra = 'in vain') is a typo for "secabis in frusta" ('into pieces'), which the English correctly renders.

notes.latin: Vestem autem sanctam, qua utetur Aaron, habebunt filii ejus post eum, ut ungantur in ea, et consecrantur manus eorum.
notes.english: The holy clothing Aaron uses shall belong to his sons after him, so that they may be anointed in it and their hands consecrated.
notes.reason: "ut ungantur in ea, et consecrantur manus eorum": the indicative appears to be a slip for the subjunctive "consecrentur", parallel to ungantur after ut. Verify against the Clementine; English is unaffected.

notes.latin: Ponesque altare contra velum, quod ante arcum pendet testimonii coram propitiatorio quo tegitur testimonium, ubi loquar tibi.
notes.english: Place the altar opposite the veil hanging before the ark of the testimony, before the atonement cover that covers the testimony, where I will speak to you.
notes.reason: "quod ante arcum pendet testimonii" (arcum = 'bow') is a typo for "ante arcam pendet testimonii" ('before the ark of the testimony'), as the English has it.

notes.latin: quam constituit Dominus Moysi in monte Sinai, quando mandabit filiis Israël ut offerrent oblationes suas Domino in deserto Sinai.
notes.english: which the Lord established for Moses on Mount Sinai, when He commanded the children of Israel to bring their offerings to the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai.
notes.reason: "quando mandabit" (future) is an apparent typo for the perfect "quando mandavit filiis Israël" (when He commanded), as the past context and the English require.

notes.latin: qui faciet unum pro peccato et alterum in holocaustum : rogabitque pro eo coram Domino, ut emundetur a fluxi seminis sui.
notes.english: The priest shall offer one for sin and the other as a whole burnt offering, and shall intercede for him before the Lord so that he may be cleansed from his flow of semen.
notes.reason: "a fluxi seminis sui" is an apparent typo; the ablative required after "a" is "a fluxu seminis sui" (from his flow of semen), as the English already renders.

notes.latin: Quem autem sacerdos emerit, et qui vernaculus domus ejus fuerit, his comedent ex eis.
notes.english: But a person the priest has bought, or a slave born in his household, may eat them.
notes.reason: "his comedent ex eis" is an apparent typo; the subject pronoun is required: "hi comedent ex eis" (these shall eat of them), as the English renders.

notes.latin: Et tamen etiam cum essent in terra hostili, non penitus abjeci eos, neque sic despexi ut consumerentur, et irritum facerent pactum meum cum eis. Ego enim sum Dominus Deus eorum,
notes.english: Yet even when they were in an enemy land, I did not utterly reject them or so despise them that they would be consumed and make My covenant with them void. For I am the Lord their God,
notes.reason: "et irritum facerent pactum meum" is probably a slip for "facerem" (and I should make void My covenant), God being the subject as in "abjeci ... despexi"; the English follows the recorded "facerent". Verify against a printed Clementine.

notes.latin: Dabisque dono Levitas
notes.english: You shall give the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons, to whom they have been handed over by the children of Israel. You shall appoint Aaron and his sons over the service of the priesthood. An outsider who approaches to minister shall die.
notes.reason: Latin truncated after "Dabisque dono Levitas"; English renders all of Vg 3:9-10. Supply: "Aaron et filiis ejus, quibus traditi sunt a filiis Israël. Aaron autem et filios ejus constitues super cultum sacerdotii. Externus, qui ad ministrandum accesserit, morietur."

notes.latin: Scribetque sacerdos in libello ista maledicta, et delebit ea aquis amarissimis, in quas maledicta congessit,
notes.english: The priest shall write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the bitter water into which he has gathered the curses, and give it to her to drink. When she has drained it, the priest shall take the sacrifice of jealousy from her hand, raise it before the Lord, and place it on the altar, provided that first he takes a handful from the sacrifice being offered and burns it on the altar; then he shall give the woman the bitter water to drink.
notes.reason: Latin gives only Vg 5:23; English renders 5:23-26. Missing: "et dabit ei bibere. Quas cum exhauserit, tollet sacerdos de manu ejus sacrificium zelotypiæ ... et sic potum det mulieri aquas amarissimas." (English also drops superlative "amarissimis".)

notes.latin: obtulit acetabulum argenteum appendens centum triginta siclos, phialam argenteam habentem septuaginta siclos, ad pondus sanctuarii, utrumque plenum simila conspersa oleo in sacrificum :
notes.english: offered a silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels and a silver bowl of seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary's weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice;
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: "in sacrificum" should read "in sacrificium" (as in 7:13, 7:19, 7:25). English is correct.

notes.latin: offeret quicumque immolaverit victimam, sacrificium similæ, decimam partem ephi, conspersæ oleo, quod mensuram habebit quartam partem hin :
notes.english: whoever sacrifices an animal shall present an offering of fine flour, a tenth of an ephah, mixed with oil measuring a quarter of a hin. He shall give wine in the same measure for pouring drink offerings with the burnt offering or sacrifice. For each lamb and ram there shall be an offering of two tenths of fine flour, mixed with a third of a hin of oil. He shall offer a third of the same measure of wine as a drink offering, as a pleasing fragrance to the Lord.
notes.reason: Latin gives only Vg 15:4; English renders 15:4-7. Missing: "et vinum ad liba fundenda ejusdem mensuræ dabit in holocaustum sive in victimam. Per agnos singulos et arietes ... offeret in odorem suavitatis Domino."

notes.latin: Sic facies
notes.english: Thus shall you do for each ox, ram, lamb, and young goat. Both native-born people and foreigners shall offer sacrifices according to the same rite. There shall be one command and judgment for both you and the sojourners in the land. The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land I will give you
notes.reason: Latin truncated after "Sic facies"; English renders Vg 15:11-18. Missing: "per singulos boves et arietes et agnos et hædos. Tam indigenæ quam peregrini eodem ritu offerent sacrificia ... Cum veneritis in terram, quam dabo vobis,"

notes.latin: oblitaque fuerit facere multitudo : offeret vitulum de armento, holocaustum in odorem suavissimum Domino, et sacrificum ejus ac liba, ut cæremoniæ postulant, hircumque pro peccato :
notes.english: and the multitude has forgotten to do it, it shall offer a young bull from the herd as a burnt offering of most pleasing fragrance to the Lord, with its grain offering and drink offerings as the ceremonies require, and a male goat for sin.
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: "et sacrificum ejus ac liba" should read "et sacrificium ejus ac liba". English is correct.

notes.latin: Cumque oriretur seditio, et tumultus incresceret,
notes.english: As rebellion arose and the uproar increased, Moses and Aaron fled to the tabernacle of the covenant. After they had entered it, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.
notes.reason: Latin gives only Vg 16:42; English also renders 16:43. Missing: "Moyses et Aaron fugerunt ad tabernaculum fœderis. Quod, postquam ingressi sunt, operuit nubes, et apparuit gloria Domini."

notes.latin: At ille respondit : Non transibis. Statimque egressus est obvius, cum infinita multitudo, et manu forti,
notes.english: But he answered: You shall not pass through. At once he came out to meet them with an immense multitude and a strong force,
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: "cum infinita multitudo" should read "cum infinita multitudine" (ablative after cum). English is correct.

notes.latin: Cumque Aaron spoliasset vestibus suis, induit eis Eleazarum filium ejus.
notes.english: After removing Aaron's garments, he put them on Eleazar his son. When Aaron had died on the mountaintop, Moses came down with Eleazar. The whole multitude, seeing that Aaron had died, wept over him for thirty days throughout all their families.
notes.reason: Latin gives only the first sentence of Vg 20:28; English renders 20:28-30. Missing: "Illo mortuo in montis supercilio, descendit cum Eleazaro. Omnis autem multitudo videns occubuisse Aaron, flevit super eo triginta diebus per cunctas familias suas."

notes.latin: Jugum ipsorum disperiit ad Hesebon usque Dibon : lassi pervenerunt in Nophe, et usque Medaba.]
notes.english: Their yoke has perished from Heshbon as far as Dibon. Exhausted, they reached Nophah and as far as Medeba.
notes.reason: Apparent typo in the Latin: "disperiit ad Hesebon usque Dibon" should read "ab Hesebon usque Dibon" (from Heshbon as far as Dibon), which the English correctly renders.

notes.latin: quæ vocaverunt eos ad sacrificia sua. At ille comederunt et adoraverunt deos earum.
notes.english: who invited them to their sacrifices. They ate and worshiped their gods.
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: "At ille comederunt" should read "At illi comederunt" (plural subject with plural verb). English is correct.

notes.latin: venerunt ad Moysen, et ad Elezarum sacerdotem, et principes multitudinis, atque dixerunt :
notes.english: they came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the multitude and said:
notes.reason: Latin has "Elezarum"; the name is spelled Eleazarus everywhere else, so read "et ad Eleazarum sacerdotem". English is correct.

notes.latin: Sculptilia eorum igne combures : non concupisces argentum et aurum, de quibus facta sunt, neque assumes ex eis tibi quidquam, ne offendas, propterea quia abominatio est Domini tui :
notes.english: Burn their carved images with fire. Do not covet the silver and gold from which they are made or take any of it for yourself, lest you fall into sin, because it is an abomination to your Lord.
notes.reason: Latin as recorded ends "abominatio est Domini tui"; the Vulgate reads "abominatio est Domini Dei tui" ("Dei" apparently dropped). English "your Lord" follows the defective text; could not verify against a printed Clementine here.

notes.latin: Audi , Israël : tu transgredieris hodie Jordanem, ut possideas nationes maximas et fortiores te, civitates ingentes, et ad cælum usque muratas,
notes.english: Hear, Israel: today you will cross the Jordan to possess nations greater and stronger than you, enormous cities walled up to heaven,
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma in the Latin: "Audi , Israël" should read "Audi, Israël".

notes.latin: et scribam in tabulis verba quæ fuerunt in his qui ante confregisti : ponesque eas in arca.
notes.english: and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the former ones you broke. Place them in the ark.
notes.reason: Latin has "in his qui ante confregisti"; the relative refers to the tablets (tabulis, feminine) and should read "in his quas ante confregisti". English is correct.

notes.latin: ut vadant et servant diis alienis, et adorent eos, solem et lunam, et omnem militiam cæli, quæ non præcepi :
notes.english: by going to serve foreign gods and worshiping them—the sun, moon, or any of the host of heaven—which I have not commanded,
notes.reason: Latin has "ut vadant et servant diis alienis"; the verb should be the subjunctive of servire: "ut vadant et serviant diis alienis". English ("to serve foreign gods") is correct.

notes.latin: Non intravit eunuchus, attritis vel amputatis testiculis et abscisso veretro, ecclesiam Domini.
notes.english: A eunuch whose testicles are crushed or cut off and whose penis is severed shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.
notes.reason: Latin has perfect 'Non intravit eunuchus' (has not entered); the Clementine reads future 'Non intrabit eunuchus', as the parallel 'ingredietur'/'intrabunt' and the English 'shall not enter' confirm. Correct to 'intrabit'.

notes.latin: loquerisque in conspectu Domini Deo tui : Abstuli quod sanctificatum est de domo mea, et dedi illud Levitæ et advenæ, et pupillo ac viduæ, sicut jussisti mihi : non præterivi mandata tua, nec sum oblitus imperii tui.
notes.english: Say before the Lord your God: I have removed the consecrated portion from my house and given it to the Levite, stranger, orphan, and widow, as You ordered me. I have not transgressed Your commandments or forgotten Your command.
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: 'in conspectu Domini Deo tui' should read 'in conspectu Domini Dei tui' (genitive, as in 26:5 and 26:10). English is correct.

notes.latin: Audite , cæli, quæ loquor : audiat terra verba oris mei.
notes.english: Hear, heavens, what I speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma: 'Audite , caeli' should read 'Audite, caeli'. The song's opening poetry bracket is also missing here although its closing ']' stands at the end of 32:3.

notes.latin: Dies autem septimo, diluculo consurgentes, circuierunt urbem, sicut dispositum erat, septies.
notes.english: On the seventh day they rose at dawn and marched around the city seven times, as had been arranged.
notes.reason: 'Dies autem septimo' is ungrammatical; the Clementine reads 'Die autem septimo, diluculo consurgentes, circuierunt urbem...'. English is correct.

notes.latin: calceamentaque perantiqua quæ ad indicium vetustatis pittaciis consuta erant, induti veteribus vestimentis : panes quoque, quos portabant ob viaticum, duri erant, et in frustra comminuti :
notes.english: They wore very old footwear, sewn with patches as a sign of age, and dressed in old clothes. The bread they carried for the journey was hard and broken into pieces.
notes.reason: 'in frustra comminuti' should be 'in frusta comminuti' (frusta, pieces; 'frustra' means in vain). English 'broken into pieces' rightly renders 'frusta'.

notes.latin: Porro filii Gerson egressa est sors, ut acciperent de tribubus Issachar et Aser et Nephthali, dimidiaque tribu Manasse in Basan, civitates numero tredecim.
notes.english: For the children of Gershon the lot came out that they should receive thirteen cities from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
notes.reason: 'Porro filii Gerson egressa est sors' should read 'Porro filiis Gerson egressa est sors' (dative, as in 'filiis Merari' in 21:7). English is correct.

notes.latin: Irruit autem spiritus Domini in Samson, et dilaceravit leonem, quasi hædum in frustra discerpens, nihil omnino habens in manu : et hoc patri et matri noluit indicare.
notes.english: The spirit of the Lord rushed upon Samson, and he tore the lion apart as though tearing a young goat into pieces, although he had nothing at all in his hand. He was unwilling to tell his father and mother about this.
notes.reason: Latin has "in frustra discerpens"; "frustra" (in vain) is a slip for "frusta" (pieces): read "in frusta discerpens". Same spelling recurs at Judges 19:29 and 20:6. The English "into pieces" is correct.

notes.latin: Quæ fundebat apud Samson lacrimas, et quærebatur, dicens : Odisti me, et non diligis : idcirco problema, quod proposuisti filiis populi mei, non vis mihi exponere. At ille respondit : Patri meo et matri nolui dicere : et tibi indicare potero ?
notes.english: She shed tears before Samson and complained, saying, “You hate me and do not love me. That is why you are unwilling to explain to me the riddle you set to the sons of my people.” He answered, “I was unwilling to tell my father and mother; can I tell you?”
notes.reason: Latin has "et quærebatur, dicens" (was being sought); the sense requires the deponent "querebatur" (complained): read "et querebatur, dicens". The English "complained" already renders the correct word.

notes.latin: Dormivit autem Samson usque ad medium noctem : et inde consurgens, apprehendit ambas portæ fores cum postibus suis et sera, impositasque humeris suis portavit ad verticem montis, qui respicit Hebron.
notes.english: Samson slept until midnight. Then he arose, seized both leaves of the gate with their posts and bar, and carried them on his shoulders to the summit of the mountain facing Hebron.
notes.reason: Latin has "usque ad medium noctem", which is ungrammatical (neuter "medium" with feminine accusative); read "usque ad medium noctis". The English "until midnight" is correct.

notes.latin: Attuleruntque ad eam satrapæ Philisthinorum septem funes, ut dixerat : quibus vinxit eam,
notes.english: The rulers of the Philistines brought her seven cords, as he had said, and she bound him with them.
notes.reason: Latin has "quibus vinxit eam" (bound her); the sense, and the English "she bound him", require the masculine: read "quibus vinxit eum".

notes.latin: Quam cum esset ingressus, arripuit gladium, et cadaver uxoris cum ossibus suis in duodecim partes ac frustra concidens, misit in omnes terminos Israël.
notes.english: When he had entered, he seized a sword, cut his wife's corpse, bones and all, into twelve parts and pieces, and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel.
notes.reason: Latin has "in duodecim partes ac frustra concidens"; "frustra" (in vain) stands for "frusta" (pieces): read "partes ac frusta". Same spelling recurs at Judges 14:6 and 20:6. The English "pieces" is correct.

notes.latin: Quam arreptam, in frustra concidi, misique partes in omnes terminos possessionis vestræ : quia numquam tantum nefas, et tam grande piaculum, factum est in Israël.
notes.english: I took her, cut her into pieces, and sent the parts throughout the territory of your possession, because never has such wickedness and so great an outrage been committed in Israel.
notes.reason: Latin has "in frustra concidi"; "frustra" (in vain) stands for "frusta" (pieces): read "in frusta concidi". Same spelling recurs at Judges 14:6 and 19:29. The English "into pieces" is correct.

notes.latin: At ille majoribus natu, et universo populo : Testes vos, inquit, estis hodie, quod possederim omnis quæ fuerunt Elimelech, et Chelion, et Mahalon, tradente Noëmi ;
notes.english: Boaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses today that I have taken possession of everything that belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon, with Naomi handing it over,
notes.reason: Latin has "quod possederim omnis quæ fuerunt"; "omnis" does not agree with neuter plural "quæ fuerunt": read "omnia quæ fuerunt Elimelech". The English "everything that belonged" is correct.

notes.latin: Vicinæ autem mulieris congratulantes ei, et dicentes : Natus est filius Noëmi : vocaverunt nomen ejus Obed : hic est pater Isai, patris David.
notes.english: The neighboring women rejoiced with her and said, “A son has been born to Naomi.” They called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
notes.reason: Latin has "Vicinæ autem mulieris congratulantes"; genitive singular "mulieris" is a slip for nominative plural: read "Vicinæ autem mulieres congratulantes ei". The English "The neighboring women" is correct.

notes.latin: Et vocabit puerum Ichabod, dicens : Translata est gloria de Israël, quia capta est arca Dei, et pro socero suo et pro viro suo ;
notes.english: She named the boy Ichabod, saying, “Glory has departed from Israel,” because the ark of God had been captured, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
notes.reason: Latin has future "Et vocabit puerum Ichabod"; the narrative requires the perfect: read "Et vocavit puerum Ichabod". The English "She named" already renders the correct form.

notes.latin: Cumque venisset Gad ad David, nuntiavit ei, dicens : Aut septem annis veniet tibi fames in terra tua : aut tribus mensibus fugies adversarios tuos, et ille te persequentur : aut certe tribus diebus erit pestilentia in terra tua. Nunc ergo delibera, et vide quem respondeam ei qui me misit sermonem.
notes.english: Gad came to David and reported to him, saying, “Either famine will come upon your land for seven years, or you will flee from your adversaries for three months while they pursue you, or there will be a plague in your land for three days. Now consider and decide what answer I shall give to Him who sent me.”
notes.reason: Latin typo: "et ille te persequentur" has singular pronoun with plural verb; the Clementine reads "et illi te persequentur". The English (they pursue you) already follows the correct text.

notes.latin: filium mulieris viduæ de tribu Nephthali, patre Tyrio, artificem ærarium, et plenum sapientia, et intelligentia, et doctrina, ad faciendum omne opus ex ære. Qui cum venisset ad regem Salomonem, fecit omne opus ejus.
notes.english: the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, whose father was a Tyrian. He was a bronze craftsman, full of wisdom, understanding, and skill for every kind of bronze work. He came to King Solomon and carried out all his work.
notes.reason: Latin begins mid-sentence ('filium mulieris viduæ'): Vg 7:13 'Misit quoque rex Salomon, et tulit Hiram de Tyro,' is absent from the record; unit #1 (site 7:1) carries Vg 7:1 instead, and site 7:38 is missing.

notes.latin: Et super capita columnarum opus in modum lilii posuit : perfectumque est opus columnarum.
notes.english: On top of the columns he placed lily-shaped work, and the work on the columns was completed.
notes.reason: Latin shown is Vg 7:22 (lily work on the columns), out of sequence between Vg 7:35 and 7:37; Vg 7:36 ('Sculpsit quoque in tabulatis illis... cherubim, et leones, et palmas...') is absent from the record.

notes.latin: Os quoque luteris intrinsecus erat in capitis summitate : et quod forinsecus apparebat, unius cubiti erat totum rotundum, pariterque habebat unum cubitum et dimidium : in angulis autem columnarum variæ cælaturæ erant : et media intercolumnia, quadrata non rotunda.
notes.english: The opening for the basin was inside the top of the frame. What appeared outside was one cubit high and entirely round, and also measured a cubit and a half across. At the corners of the uprights were various carvings, while the spaces between the uprights were square, not round.
notes.reason: Latin shown is Vg 7:31 (mouth of the laver), out of sequence between Vg 7:44 and 7:47; Vg 7:45 ('Et lebetes, et scutras, et hamulas: omnia vasa quæ fecit Hiram... de aurichalco erant') is absent.

notes.latin: Convertitque rex faciem suam, et benedixit omni ecclesiæ Israël : omnia enim ecclesia Israël stabat.
notes.english: The king turned his face and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood.
notes.reason: Typo 'omnia enim ecclesia Israël stabat': the Clementine reads 'omnis enim ecclesia Israël stabat' (nominative feminine singular agreeing with 'ecclesia').

notes.latin: Tunc ait Salomon : Dominus dixit ut habitaret in nebula.
notes.english: Then Solomon said, “The Lord said He would dwell in a cloud.
notes.reason: Vg 8:12 is recorded a second time here (already unit #60 at site 8:12), so the verse is duplicated in the column; the English also ends with an unclosed quotation mark.

notes.latin: Filia autem Pharaonis ascendit de civitate David in domum suam, quam ædificaverat ei Salomon : tunc ædificavit Mello.
notes.english: Pharaoh's daughter went up from the City of David to her house, which Solomon had built for her. Then he built the Millo.
notes.reason: Vg 9:24 is recorded twice in the column: here at site 9:9a and again, identically, at unit #25 (site 9:24). Duplicated verse.

notes.latin: Hæc est summa expensarum quam obtulit rex Salomon ad ædificandam domum Domini et domum suam, et Mello, et murum Jerusalem, et Heser, et Mageddo, et Gazer.
notes.english: This is the account of the expenses King Solomon incurred to build the Lord's house, his own house, the Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
notes.reason: Units #52-#54 (site 10:22a-c) repeat Vg 9:15, 9:20, 9:22, already shown at #16, #21, #23. #53 also breaks off mid-sentence: its main clause is Vg 9:21 ('horum filios... fecit Salomon tributarios'), not shown there.

notes.latin: Dormivitque Salomon cum patribus suis, et sepultus est in civitate David patris sui : regnavitque Roboam filius ejus pro eo.
notes.english: Solomon slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam reigned in his place.
notes.reason: Units #25-#44 (site 12:24a-z) repeat Vulgate verses shown elsewhere (Vg 11:26, 11:29, 11:40, 11:43, 12:4-24, 14:1-17); Vg 11:43 'Dormivitque Salomon...' appears twice within the run (#25 and #28). Duplicated verses.

notes.latin: idcirco ecce ego inducam mala super domum Jeroboam, et percutiam de Jeroboam mingentem ad parietem, et clausum, et novissimum in Israël : et mundabo reliquias domus Jeroboam, sicut mundari solet fimus usque ad purum.
notes.english: Therefore, behold, I will bring calamity upon Jeroboam's house. I will strike down every one of Jeroboam's men who urinates against a wall, the confined and the last remaining in Israel. I will sweep away the remnants of Jeroboam's house as dung is swept away until all is clean.
notes.reason: Latin begins mid-sentence with 'idcirco ecce ego inducam' (Vg 14:10): the grounds in Vg 14:7-9 are not shown, so 'Therefore' has no antecedent; #35 (Vg 14:17) likewise ends on a comma, 'puer mortuus est,'.

notes.latin: Stetique cum eo, et conturbatus est usque ad suffusionem vultus : flevitque vir Dei.
notes.english: He stood with him, and he grew troubled until his face flushed. The man of God wept.
notes.reason: Latin has "Stetique" (which would be first person, 'and I stood'); the Clementine reads "Stetitque cum eo" ('and he stood with him'), as the English correctly renders. Correct Latin: Stetitque.

notes.latin: At ille responderunt : Falsum est, sed magis narra nobis. Qui ait eis : Hæc et hæc locutus est mihi, et ait : Hæc dicit Dominus : Unxi te regem super Israël.
notes.english: They answered, “That is not true. Tell us instead.” He said to them, “He said such and such to me, and told me, ‘Thus says the Lord: I have anointed you king over Israel.’”
notes.reason: Latin has singular "At ille responderunt" with a plural verb; the Clementine reads "At illi responderunt" ('But they answered'). Correct Latin: At illi responderunt.

notes.latin: Rescripsit autem eis litteras secundo, dicens : Si mei estis, et obeditis mihi, tollite capita filiorum domini vestri, et venite ad me hac eadem hora cras in Jezrahel. Porro filii regis, septuaginta viri, apud optimates civitates nutriebantur.
notes.english: He wrote a second letter to them: “If you are mine and obey me, take the heads of your master's sons and come to me at Jezreel tomorrow at this same hour.” The king's sons, seventy men, were being brought up by the city's nobles.
notes.reason: Latin has "apud optimates civitates nutriebantur"; the Clementine reads genitive "civitatis" ('with the nobles of the city'), as the English renders. Correct Latin: apud optimates civitatis.

notes.latin: Cumque venissent litteras ad eos, tulerunt filios regis, et occiderunt septuaginta viros, et posuerunt capita eorum in cophinis, et miserunt ad eum in Jezrahel.
notes.english: When the letter reached them, they took the king's sons and killed the seventy men. They put their heads in baskets and sent them to him at Jezreel.
notes.reason: Latin has accusative "Cumque venissent litteras ad eos"; the subject must be nominative: Clementine "Cumque venissent litteræ ad eos" ('when the letter reached them').

notes.latin: Percussit autem Dominus regem, et fuit leprosus usque in diem mortis suæ, et habitabat in domo libera seorsum : Joatham vero filius regis gubernabat palatium, et judicabit populum terræ.
notes.english: The Lord struck the king, and he was a leper until the day of his death. He lived apart in a separate house, while Jotham the king's son governed the palace and was to judge the people of the land.
notes.reason: Latin has future "judicabit populum terræ" beside imperfect "gubernabat"; the Clementine reads "judicabat" ('judged'). Correct Latin: et judicabat populum terræ. The English 'was to judge' appears to follow the slip.

notes.latin: Sellum filius Jabes regnavit trigesimo novo anno Azariæ regis Juda : regnavit autem uno mense in Samaria.
notes.english: Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, and reigned one month in Samaria.
notes.reason: Latin has "trigesimo novo anno" ('thirty-new year'); the Clementine reads "trigesimo nono anno" ('thirty-ninth year'), as the English renders. Correct Latin: trigesimo nono anno.

notes.latin: Iste est sermo, quem locutus est Dominus de eo : [Sprevit te, et subsannavit te, virgo filia Sion : post tergum tuum caput movit, filia Jerusalem.
notes.english: This is the word the Lord has spoken concerning him: The virgin daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind your back.
notes.reason: Stray markup: an opening square bracket before "Sprevit" ("[Sprevit te"), with its closing bracket after "servum meum." in 19:34 (#34). Source-edition verse brackets, not Latin text. Correct Latin: Sprevit te ... servum meum.

notes.latin: Reliqua autem sermonum Manasse, ut universa quæ fecit, et peccatum ejus quod peccavit, nonne hæc scripta sunt in libro sermonum dierum regum Juda ?
notes.english: The rest of the acts of Manasseh, everything he did, and the sin he committed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
notes.reason: Latin has "Manasse, ut universa quæ fecit"; the Clementine reads "et universa quæ fecit" ('and everything he did'), as the English renders. Correct Latin: et universa quæ fecit.

notes.latin: Ierunt itaque Helcias sacerdos, et Ahicam, et Achobor, et Sapham, et Asaia, ad Holdam prophetidem, uxorem Sellum filii Thecuæ filii Araas custodis vestium, quæ habitabat in Jerusalem in Secunda : locutique sunt ad eam.
notes.english: Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the garments. She lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter. They spoke to her.
notes.reason: Latin has "et Sapham" for the scribe named "Saphan" in 22:3, 8-10, 12; apparent typo. Correct Latin: et Saphan. English 'Shaphan' is right.

notes.latin: Et ait : Dimitte eum : nemo commoveat ossa ejus. Et intacta manserunt ossa illius cum ossibus prophetæ qui venerat de Samaria.
notes.english: He said, “Leave him alone. Let no one disturb his bones.” His bones remained untouched, together with the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria.
notes.reason: Latin has singular "Dimitte eum", though Josiah addresses the citizens (plural "Responderunt... cives"); the Clementine reads plural "Dimittite eum". Apparent truncation. Correct Latin: Dimittite eum. English is unaffected.

notes.latin: Adam , Seth, Enos,
notes.english: Adam, Seth, Enosh,
notes.reason: Stray space before the first comma ("Adam , Seth"), probably left by stripped markup. Correct Latin: Adam, Seth, Enos,

notes.latin: Noë, Sem, Cham, et Japtheth.
notes.english: Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
notes.reason: Typo "Japtheth"; the Clementine reads "Japheth" (as in 1:5, "Filii Japheth"). Correct Latin: Noë, Sem, Cham, et Japheth.

notes.latin: De tribu Issachar, Cedes et suburbanis suis, et Dabereth cum suburbanis suis,
notes.english: From the tribe of Issachar: Kedesh with its pasturelands, Daberath with its pasturelands,
notes.reason: 'Cedes et suburbanis suis' is ungrammatical (ablative without 'cum'); the Clementine reads 'Cedes et suburbana ejus, et Dabereth cum suburbanis suis'.

notes.latin: Filiis autem Merari residuis : de tribu Zabulon, Remmono et suburbana ejus, et Thabor cum suburbanis sus :
notes.english: To the remaining sons of Merari, from the tribe of Zebulun: Rimmono and its pasturelands, and Tabor with its pasturelands.
notes.reason: Typo 'cum suburbanis sus'; should read 'et Thabor cum suburbanis suis'.

notes.latin: Benedictus Dominus Deus Israël, ab æterno usque in æternum.] Et dicat omnis populo : Amen, et hymnum Domino.
notes.english: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from eternity to eternity.” And let all the people say, “Amen,” and sing a hymn to the Lord.
notes.reason: 'Et dicat omnis populo' is a typo; the Clementine reads 'Et dicat omnis populus : Amen, et hymnum Domino.'

notes.latin: Transibant autem multi dies in Israël absque Deo vero, et absque sacerdote doctore, et absque lege.
notes.english: Many days passed in Israel without the true God, without a priest to teach, and without the law.
notes.reason: "Transibant" is probably a slip for Clementine "Transibunt" (future, matching "reperient" and "non erit" in vv. 4-5). The English "passed" follows the Latin as recorded; check the Latin source.

notes.latin: pugnavit enim gens contra gentem, et civitas contra civitatem, quia Dominus conturbabit eos in omni angustia.
notes.english: Nation fought against nation and city against city, for the Lord will trouble them with every distress.
notes.reason: "pugnavit" is probably a b/v slip for Clementine "pugnabit" (future, beside "conturbabit" in the same verse). The English "fought" follows the Latin as recorded; check the Latin source.

notes.latin: Et ambulavit in via patris suis Asa, nec declinavit ab ea, faciens quæ placita erant coram Domino.
notes.english: He walked in the way of his father Asa and did not depart from it, doing what was pleasing before the Lord.
notes.reason: "in via patris suis Asa" is ungrammatical; the Clementine reads "in via patris sui Asa". The English is unaffected.

notes.latin: Et congregavit virtutem, et exercitum fortem nimis : et exaltatum est, et elevatum cor ejus :
notes.english: He gathered a powerful force and an exceedingly strong army, and his heart was exalted and lifted up.
notes.reason: Verse truncated: Vulgate 1:5 ("Et obtinuit regiones gentium, et tyrannos : et facti sunt illi in tributum") is absent in Latin and English; the next unit is already Vg 1:6.

notes.latin: Et convertit Antiochus, postquam percussit Ægyptum in centesimo et quadragesimo tertio anno : et ascendit ad Israël,
notes.english: After striking Egypt in the one hundred forty-third year, Antiochus returned and went up against Israel.
notes.reason: Verse truncated: Latin ends on a comma; Vulgate 1:22 ("et ascendit Jerosolymam in multitudine gravi") is absent in Latin and English; the next unit is Vg 1:23.

notes.latin: Et locutus est ad eos verba pacifica in dolo : et crediderunt ei.
notes.english: He spoke peaceful words to them deceitfully, and they believed him.
notes.reason: Verse truncated: Vulgate 1:32 ("et irruit super civitatem repente, et percussit eam plaga magna, et perdidit populum multum ex Israël") is absent in Latin and English; the next unit is Vg 1:33.

notes.latin: et prohiberent holocausta et sacrificia, et placationes fieri in templo Dei,
notes.english: to forbid burnt offerings, sacrifices, and propitiatory offerings in the temple of God,
notes.reason: Verse truncated: Latin ends on a comma; Vulgate 1:48 ("et prohiberent celebrari sabbatum, et dies solemnes") is absent in Latin and English; the next unit is Vg 1:49.

notes.latin: Secundum omnia verba hæc scripsit omni regno suo : et præposuit principes populo, qui hæc fieri cogerent.
notes.english: According to all these words he wrote to his whole kingdom, and he set rulers over the people to compel them to do these things.
notes.reason: Verse truncated: Vulgate 1:54 ("et jusserunt civitatibus Juda sacrificare") is absent in Latin and English; the next unit is Vg 1:55.

notes.latin: Et audivit Alexander rex, et contristatus est valde, et reversus est Antiochum.
notes.english: King Alexander heard and was greatly distressed, and returned to Antioch.
notes.reason: Latin as recorded reads "reversus est Antiochum" (a person's name, accusative); the Clementine reads "reversus est Antiochiam" (to Antioch), which the English correctly renders. Correct the Latin to "Antiochiam".

notes.latin: Et quæsierunt omnes gentes quæ erant in circuitu eorum conterere eos : dixerunt enim :
notes.english: All the nations around them sought to crush them, for they said,
notes.reason: Verse truncated: Latin and English stop at "dixerunt enim :" / "for they said,". The speech, Vulgate 12:54 ("Non habent principem, et adjuvantem : nunc ergo expugnemus illos, et tollamus de hominibus memoriam eorum"), is absent from the chunk.

notes.latin: Et constituit ut omnibus annis agerentur dies hi cum lætitia.
notes.english: He decreed that these days should be celebrated with joy every year.
notes.reason: Verse truncated: Vulgate 13:53 ("Et munivit montem templi, qui erat secus arcem, et habitavit ibi ipse, et qui cum eo erant") is absent in Latin and English; the next unit is already Vg 13:54.

notes.latin: Cumque retulisset ad regem Apollonius de pecuniis quæ delatæ erant, illæ accitum Heliodorum, qui erat super negotia ejus, misit, cum mandatis ut prædictam pecuniam transportaret.
notes.english: When Apollonius reported to the king the money that had been disclosed, the king summoned Heliodorus, who was in charge of his affairs, and sent him with orders to carry away the aforesaid money.
notes.reason: Latin has "illæ accitum Heliodorum"; "illæ" (feminine plural) has no construction. Read "ille accitum Heliodorum ... misit" (he, the king, summoned and sent Heliodorus). English already renders "ille".

notes.latin: Statimque Heliodorus iter est agressus, specie quidem quasi per Cœlesyriam et Phœnicen civitates esset peragraturus, re vera autem regis propositum perfecturus.
notes.english: Heliodorus immediately set out, ostensibly to visit the cities throughout Coelesyria and Phoenicia, but actually to accomplish the king's purpose.
notes.reason: Apparent misspelling in the Latin: "iter est agressus" should read "iter est aggressus" (set out on the journey). English is unaffected.

notes.latin: misit Jason facinorosus ab Jerosolymis viros peccatores, portantes argenti didrachmas trecentas in sacrificum Herculis : quas postulaverunt hi qui asportaverant ne in sacrificiis erogarentur, quia non oporteret, sed in alios sumptus eas deputari. · Translation note. Didrachms are retained as the named denomination; no modern currency or fixed wage equivalent is substituted.
notes.english: the criminal Jason sent sinful men from Jerusalem carrying three hundred silver didrachms for a sacrifice to Hercules. Those who carried them requested that they not be spent on sacrifices, since that was not proper, but assigned to other expenses.
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: "in sacrificum Herculis" should read "in sacrificium Herculis" (for the sacrifice of Hercules). English is unaffected.

notes.latin: nam ad hunc exactio vectigalium pertinebant : quam ob causam utrique ad regem sunt evocati.
notes.english: For the collection of revenues belonged to him; for this reason both men were summoned to the king.
notes.reason: Number slip in the Latin: "ad hunc exactio vectigalium pertinebant" has a plural verb with singular subject "exactio"; read "pertinebat". English is unaffected.

notes.latin: Sed cum falsus rumor exisset, tamquam vita excessisset Antiochus, assumptis Jason non minus mille viris, repente agressus est civitatem : et civibus ad murum convolantibus ad ultimum apprehensa civitate, Menelaus fugit in arcem :
notes.english: When a false report spread that Antiochus had died, Jason took no fewer than a thousand men and suddenly attacked the city. As the citizens rushed to the wall, the city was finally taken, and Menelaus fled into the citadel.
notes.reason: Apparent misspelling in the Latin: "repente agressus est civitatem" should read "aggressus est" (same spelling recurs at 3:8). English is unaffected.

notes.latin: Videns autem Philippus paulatim virum ad profectum venire, ac frequentius res ei cedere propere, ad Ptolemæum ducem Cœlesyriæ et Phœnicis scripsit ut auxilium ferret regis negotiis.
notes.english: Philip saw the man gradually advancing and his affairs going swiftly in his favor with increasing frequency, and wrote to Ptolemy, governor of Coelesyria and Phoenicia, to bring aid to the king's affairs.
notes.reason: Latin has "res ei cedere propere" (hastily); the Clementine reads "cedere prospere" (turn out prosperously). The English "going swiftly in his favor" follows the defective "propere" and should be rechecked once the Latin is corrected.

notes.latin: Ora itaque vos, et peto memores beneficiorum publice et privatim, ut unusquisque conservet fidem ad me et ad filium meum.
notes.english: I therefore beg and ask you, remembering the benefits you have received publicly and privately, that each of you maintain loyalty to me and my son.
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: "Ora itaque vos, et peto" should read "Oro itaque vos, et peto" (I beg and ask you). English already renders "Oro".

notes.latin: Machab æus autem, et qui cum eo erant, Domino se protegente, templum quidem et civitatem recepit : · Translation note. The accessed Latin has a typographic split within Machabæus (“Machab æus”). The Latin column preserves the canonical extraction; the English treats it as the single proper name Maccabeus.
notes.english: Maccabeus and those with him recovered the temple and the city, with the Lord protecting him.
notes.reason: Split word in the Latin: "Machab æus autem" should read "Machabæus autem" (the unit's own note acknowledges the split). English is unaffected.

notes.latin: De quibus autem ad regem judicavit referendum, confestim aliquem mittere, diligentius inter vos conferentes, ut decernamus, sicut congruit vobis : nos enim Antiochiam accedimus.
notes.english: As for the matters he judged should be referred to the king, discuss them carefully among yourselves and immediately send someone, so that we may decide what is suitable for you; for we are on our way to Antioch.
notes.reason: Latin has the infinitive "confestim aliquem mittere", which has no construction; the Clementine reads the imperative "confestim aliquem mittite" (send someone at once). English already renders the imperative.

notes.latin: Sed post triennii tempus, cognovit Judas et qui cum eo erant Demetrium Seleuci cum multitudine valida et navibus per portam Tripolis ascendisse ad loca opportuna,
notes.english: After three years, Judas and those with him learned that Demetrius son of Seleucus had come up through the harbor of Tripolis with a strong force and ships, to suitable positions,
notes.reason: Latin has "per portam Tripolis" (through the gate); the Clementine reads "per portum Tripolis" (through the harbor), which the English "through the harbor of Tripolis" already renders.

notes.latin: Itaque omnes communi consilio decreverunt nullo modo diem istum absque celebritate præterire :
notes.english: All therefore decreed by common counsel that this day should by no means pass without celebration,
notes.reason: Vulgate 15:37 is missing between this unit and the next (Vg 15:38): "habere autem celebritatem tertiadecima die mensis Adar, quod dicitur voce syriaca, pridie Mardochæi diei." Latin and English both break off at "præterire :" / "celebration,".

notes.latin: A me ergo positum est decretum : ut omnis homo qui hanc mutaverit jussionem, tollatur lignum de domum ipsius, et erigatur, et configatur in eo, domus autem ejus publicetur.
notes.english: I have also issued this decree: whoever alters this command shall have a timber taken from his house, erected, and himself fastened upon it; his house shall be confiscated.
notes.reason: Latin has "de domum ipsius"; "de" takes the ablative and the Clementine reads "tollatur lignum de domo ipsius". Apparent typo; English is unaffected.

notes.latin: De filii Begui, Uthai et Zachur, et cum eis septuaginta viri.
notes.english: Of the descendants of Bigvai, Uthai and Zaccur, and with them seventy men.
notes.reason: Latin has "De filii Begui"; should read "De filiis Begui, Uthai et Zachur" (ablative plural, as in every parallel verse of the list). English is unaffected.

notes.ref: Job 23:15 (card shown on 2 rows, to Job 23:15a)
notes.latin: Et idcirco a facie ejus turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor.
notes.english: Therefore I am troubled before His face, and when I consider Him, I am troubled with fear.
notes.reason: Vg 23:14 is missing from the record: units pass from 23:13 to 23:15. Latin wanting: "Cum expleverit in me voluntatem suam, et alia multa similia præsto sunt ei." This unit itself is rendered correctly.

notes.latin: Hæc est pars hominis impii apud Deum, et hæreditas violentorum, quam ob Omnipotente suscipient.
notes.english: This is the wicked man's portion with God and the inheritance that the violent shall receive from the Almighty.
notes.reason: Typo "quam ob Omnipotente suscipient": read "quam ab Omnipotente suscipient" (ab with ablative; English "from the Almighty" already renders ab).

notes.latin: Davidi , cum immutavit vultum suum coram Achimelech, et dimisit eum, et abiit.
notes.english: For David, when he changed his appearance before Ahimelech, who dismissed him, and he went away.
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma in "Davidi , cum immutavit"; read "Davidi, cum immutavit vultum suum coram Achimelech, et dimisit eum, et abiit."

notes.ref: Psalms 71:1 (card shown on 2 rows, to Psalms 71:2)
notes.latin: Psalmus , in Salomonem.
notes.english: A psalm concerning Solomon. God, give Your judgment to the king and Your righteousness to the king's son, to judge Your people with righteousness and Your poor with judgment.

notes.english: You shall speak all these words to them, but they will not listen to you; you shall call them, but they will not answer you.
notes.reason: Card serves rows 7:27 and 7:28 but Latin and English give only v.27; Vg 7:28 ("Et dices ad eos: Hæc est gens quæ non audivit vocem Domini Dei sui…") is absent.

notes.latin: Quod facum est verbum Domini ad Jeremiam prophetam adversus Ælam, in principio regni Sedeciæ regis Juda, dicens :
notes.english: The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet against Elam, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: "Quod facum est verbum Domini" should read "Quod factum est verbum Domini".

notes.latin: Ideo ecce dies veniunt, dicit Dominus, et auditum faciam super Rabbath filiorum Ammon fremitum prælii, et erit in tumultum dissipata, filiæque ejus igni succendentur, et possidebit Israël possessores suos, ait Dominus.
notes.english: Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make the roar of battle heard against Rabbah of the Ammonites. She will be scattered in tumult, and her daughters will be burned with fire. Israel will possess those who possessed him, says the Lord.
notes.reason: "erit in tumultum dissipata" is probably a slip for "in tumulum dissipata" ('destroyed into a heap', as Douay renders); the English 'scattered in tumult' follows the recorded form. Verify against a printed Clementine.

notes.latin: Persecutus est autem Chadæorum exercitus regem, et apprehenderunt Sedeciam in deserto quod est juxta Jericho : et omnis comitatus ejus diffugit ab eo.
notes.english: The Chaldean army pursued the king and captured Zedekiah in the wilderness near Jericho. All his companions had scattered from him.
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: 'Chadæorum' should read 'Chaldæorum' ('Persecutus est autem Chaldæorum exercitus regem'). The English is correct.

notes.ref: Daniel 1:44 (Vulgate 13:44) (card shown on 2 rows, to Daniel 1:45)
notes.latin: Exaudivit autem Dominus vocem ejus.
notes.english: The Lord heard her voice.
notes.reason: Card shown on rows 1:44-1:45 holds only Vg 13:44. The Latin of 13:45 is absent: 'Cumque duceretur ad mortem, suscitavit Dominus spiritum sanctum pueri junioris, cujus nomen Daniel :'. English likewise covers only verse 44.

notes.ref: Daniel 1:60 (Vulgate 13:60) (card shown on 3 rows, to Daniel 1:62)
notes.latin: Exclamavit itaque omnis cœtus voce magna, et benedixerunt Deum, qui salvat sperantes in se.
notes.english: The whole assembly cried out with a loud voice and blessed God, who saves those who hope in Him.
notes.reason: Card shown on rows 1:60-1:62 holds only Vg 13:60. The Latin of 13:61-62 (the elders convicted by Daniel 'ex ore suo' and put to death, 'et salvatus est sanguis innoxius in die illa') is absent, as is its English.

notes.ref: Daniel 5:26 (card shown on 3 rows, to Daniel 5:28)
notes.latin: Et hæc est interpretatio sermonis. Mane : numeravit Deus regnum tuum, et complevit illud.
notes.english: And this is the meaning of the message: ‘Mane’: God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end.
notes.reason: Card shown on rows 5:26-5:28 holds only verse 26. Latin of 27-28 is absent: 'Thecel : appensus es in statera, et inventus es minus habens. Phares : divisum est regnum tuum, et datum est Medis et Persis.' English likewise stops at 'Mane'.

notes.latin: Et levavi oculus meos, et vidi : et ecce aries unus stabat ante paludem, habens cornua excelsa, et unum excelsius altero atque succrescens. Postea
notes.english: I lifted my eyes and looked, and behold, a ram stood before the marsh. It had high horns, one higher than the other and still growing. Afterward,
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: 'levavi oculus meos' should read 'levavi oculos meos'.

notes.latin: Et venit rex aquilonis, et comportabit aggerem, et capiet urbes munitissimas : et brachia austri non sustinebunt, et consurgent electi ejus ad resistendum, et non erit fortitudo.
notes.english: The king of the north will come, heap up a siege ramp, and capture strongly fortified cities. The forces of the south will not withstand him. His chosen men will arise to resist, but they will have no strength.
notes.reason: 'Et venit rex aquilonis' appears to be a slip for the Clementine future 'Et veniet rex aquilonis' (parallel to 'comportabit', 'capiet'); the English already renders the future.

notes.latin: Et seminabo eam mihi in terra, et miserebor ejus quæ fuit Absque misericordia.
notes.english: I will sow her for Myself in the land, and I will have mercy on her who was Without Mercy.
notes.reason: Unit stops at Vg 2:23; Vg 2:24 (second half of Heb 2:25) is absent from Latin and English: 'Et dicam Non populo meo : Populus meus es tu ; et ipse dicet : Deus meus es tu.'

notes.latin: Super capita montium sacrificabant, et super colles ascendebant thymiama ; subtus quercum, et populum, et terebinthum, quia bona erat umbra ejus ; ideo fornicabuntur filiæ vestræ, et sponsæ vestræ adulteræ erunt.
notes.english: They sacrificed on the mountaintops and sent incense up on the hills, beneath oak and poplar and terebinth, because its shade was good. Therefore your daughters will prostitute themselves, and your brides will commit adultery.
notes.reason: 'ascendebant thymiama' appears to be a slip for the Vulgate's 'accendebant thymiama' (they burned incense); English 'sent incense up' follows the faulty form. Verify against a printed Clementine.

notes.latin: In tribulatione sua mane consurgent ad me : Venite, et revertamur ad Dominum,
notes.english: In their affliction they will rise early to Me: “Come, let us return to the Lord,
notes.reason: Vg 6:2 is missing from Latin and English between this unit and the next (Vg 6:3): 'quia ipse cepit, et sanabit nos ; percutiet, et curabit nos.' The unit breaks off at 'revertamur ad Dominum,'.

notes.latin: Et tollet eum propinquus suus, et comburet eum, ut efferat ossa de domo ; et dicet ei, qui in penetralibus domus est : Numquid adhuc est penes te ?
notes.english: His relative will take him up and burn him, to bring the bones out of the house. He will say to the one in the house's inner chambers, “Is anyone still with you?”
notes.reason: Vg 6:11 is missing from Latin and English between this unit (Vg 6:10) and the next (Vg 6:12): 'Et respondebit : Finis est. Et dicet ei : Tace, et non recorderis nominis Domini.'

notes.latin: Numquid super isto non commovebitur terra, et lugebit omnis habitator ejus, et ascendet quasi fluvius universus, et ejicicetur, et defluet, quasi rivus Ægypti ?
notes.english: Will the land not shake over this, and every inhabitant of it mourn? It will rise up, all of it, like a river, be cast out, and sink down like the stream of Egypt.
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: 'ejicicetur' should be 'ejicietur' (et ejicietur, et defluet).

notes.latin: Et dixi : Audite, princeps Jacob, et duces domus Israël : numquid non vestrum est scire judicium,
notes.english: I said: “Hear, prince of Jacob and leaders of the house of Israel! Is it not your part to know justice,
notes.reason: 'Audite, princeps Jacob' looks like a slip for the Vulgate's plural 'principes Jacob' (plural 'Audite', 'vestrum'; cf. 3:9 'principes domus Jacob'). English 'prince of Jacob' follows the singular. Verify against a printed Clementine.

notes.latin: Et confundentur qui vident visiones, et confundentur divini ; et operient omnes vultos suos, quia non est responsum Dei.
notes.english: Those who see visions will be ashamed, and the diviners confounded; they will all cover their faces, because there is no answer from God.”
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: 'omnes vultos suos' should be 'omnes vultus suos' (fourth-declension accusative plural).

notes.latin: Convenite , congregamini, gens non amabilis,
notes.english: Come together, gather yourselves, unlovable nation,
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma in the Latin: 'Convenite , congregamini' should be 'Convenite, congregamini, gens non amabilis,'.

notes.latin: Quam, cum impleta esset, educentes, et secus littus sedentes, elegerunt bonis in vasa, malos autem foras miserunt.
notes.english: Which, when it was filled, they drew out, and sitting by the shore, they chose out the good into vessels, but the bad they cast forth.
notes.reason: Latin typo: "elegerunt bonis in vasa" should read "elegerunt bonos in vasa" (accusative object, parallel to "malos autem"). English is correct.

notes.latin: Et factum est iterum Dominus sabbatis ambularet per sata, et discipuli ejus cœperunt progredi, et vellere spicas.
notes.english: And it happened again, as the Lord walked through the grain fields on the sabbath, that his disciples began to go forward and to pluck the ears of grain.
notes.reason: Latin has lost "cum": the subjunctive "ambularet" has no conjunction. Clementine reads "Et factum est iterum cum Dominus sabbatis ambularet per sata"; the English ("as the Lord walked") renders the full text.

notes.latin: quia non intrat in cor ejus, sed in ventrum vadit, et in secessum exit, purgans omnes escas?
notes.english: because it does not enter his heart, but goes into the belly and passes into the latrine, purging all foods?
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: "in ventrum vadit" should be "in ventrem vadit" (accusative of venter). English "into the belly" is right.

notes.latin: et suscipiens in cælum, ingemuit, et ait illi: Ephphetha, quod est, Adaperire.
notes.english: And looking up to heaven, he groaned and said to him: Ephpheta, which is, Be opened.
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: "suscipiens in cælum" (receiving) should be "suspiciens in cælum" (looking up), as the Clementine reads and as the English "looking up to heaven" renders.

notes.latin: Et responderunt ei discipuli sui: Unde illos quis poterit saturare panibus in solitudine?
notes.english: And his disciples answered him: From where can anyone fill them here with bread in the wilderness?
notes.reason: English "here" has no counterpart in the Latin shown; the Clementine appears to read "quis poterit hic saturare panibus", so "hic" seems dropped from the record. If the Latin stands as recorded, delete "here".

notes.latin: Quo cognito, ait illis Jesus: Quid cogitatis, quia panes non habetis? nondum cognoscetis nec intelligitis? adhuc cæcatum habetis cor vestrum?
notes.english: Which Jesus knowing, says to them: Why do you reason, because you have no bread? Do you not yet know nor understand? Have you still your heart blinded?
notes.reason: "nondum cognoscetis" (future) looks like a typo for the Clementine's present "nondum cognoscitis nec intelligitis"; the English "Do you not yet know" renders the present.

notes.latin: Qui sciens versutiam illorum, ait illos: Quid me tentatis? afferte mihi denarium ut videam.
notes.english: Who knowing their wiliness, says to them: Why tempt you me? Bring me a denarius that I may see it.
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: "ait illos" should be "ait illis" (dative), as the Clementine reads; English "says to them" is right.

notes.latin: Et respondens Jesus cœpit dicere illis: Videte ne quid vos seducat:
notes.english: And Jesus answering, began to say to them: Take care lest any man deceive you.
notes.reason: "ne quid vos seducat" (lest anything deceive you) looks like a typo for the Clementine's "ne quis vos seducat", which the English "lest any man deceive you" renders.

notes.latin: Erat autem qui dicebatur Barrabas, qui cum seditiosis erat vinctus, qui in seditione fecerat homicidium.
notes.english: And there was one called Barabbas, who was put in prison with some seditious men, who in the sedition had committed murder.
notes.reason: Latin has 'Barrabas', against 'Barabbam' in 15:11 and 15:15; apparently a misspelling of 'Barabbas' (possibly inherited from the source edition). English 'Barabbas' is correct.

notes.latin: Beati eritis cum vos oderint homines, et cum separaverint vos, et exprobraverint, et ejicerint nomen vestrum tamquam malum propter Filium hominis.
notes.english: Blessed shall you be when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you and shall reproach you and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of Man’s sake.
notes.reason: Latin has 'ejicerint', not a valid form; the future perfect parallel to 'separaverint' and 'exprobraverint' is 'ejecerint'. English 'cast out' is correct.

notes.latin: Nolite judicare, et non judicabimini: nolite condemnare, et non condemnabimini. Dimitte, et dimittemini.
notes.english: Judge not: and you shall not be judged. Condemn not: and you shall not be condemned. Forgive: and you shall be forgiven.
notes.reason: Latin has singular 'Dimitte, et dimittemini' amid plural imperatives and a plural passive; the Clementine reads 'Dimittite, et dimittemini'. English 'Forgive: and you shall be forgiven' is correct.

notes.latin: et mulieres aliquæ, quæ erant curatæ a spiritibus malignis et infirmatibus: Maria, quæ vocatur Magdalene, de qua septem dæmonia exierant,
notes.english: And certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary who is called Magdalen, out of whom seven demons had gone forth,
notes.reason: Latin typo 'infirmatibus'; read 'infirmitatibus' ('a spiritibus malignis et infirmitatibus'). English 'infirmities' is correct.

notes.latin: Factum est autem cum rediisset Jesus, excepit illum turba: erunt enim omnes exspectantes eum.
notes.english: And it happened that when Jesus was returned, the multitude received him: for they were all waiting for him.
notes.reason: Latin typo 'erunt enim omnes exspectantes eum' (future); read 'erant enim omnes exspectantes eum'. English 'they were all waiting' is correct.

notes.latin: Qui dixit illis: Ubicumque fuerit corpus, illuc congregabuntur et aquilæ.
notes.english: Who said to them: Wherever the body shall be, there will the eagles also be gathered together.
notes.reason: Vg 17:36 'Respondentes dicunt illi: Ubi Domine?' is missing: no unit between 17:35 and 17:37 carries it, so 'Qui dixit illis' lacks the disciples' question in both Latin and English.

notes.latin: Et erat docens quotidie in templo. Principes autem sacerdotum, et scribæ, et princeps plebis quærebant illum perdere:
notes.english: And he was teaching daily in the temple. And the chief priests and the scribes and the ruler of the people sought to destroy him.
notes.reason: Recorded 'princeps plebis' (singular) appears to be a slip for the Clementine 'principes plebis' (plural, with 'quærebant'); if corrected, English 'the ruler of the people' should read 'the rulers of the people'. Verify against a printed Clementine.

notes.latin: neque enim ultra mori potuerunt: æquales enim angelis sunt, et filii sunt Dei, cum sint filii resurrectionis.
notes.english: Neither can they die any more for they are equal to the angels and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection.
notes.reason: Recorded 'mori potuerunt' (perfect) appears to be a typo for the Clementine 'mori poterunt' (future: 'neither shall they be able to die any more'), parallel to 'nubent', 'ducent'. English is unaffected.

notes.latin: Exclamavit autem simul universa turba, dicens: Tolle hunc, et dimitte nobis Barabbam:
notes.english: But the whole multitude together cried out, saying: Away with this man, and release to us Barabbas:
notes.reason: Clementine Luke 23:17 ('Necesse autem habebat dimittere eis per diem festum unum') is absent from the record: units pass from 23:16 to 23:18 with neither Latin nor English for it.

notes.latin: Erat autem quidam homo ibi triginta et octo annos habens in infirmitate sua.
notes.english: And there was a certain man there that had been eight and thirty years under his infirmity.
notes.reason: Clementine John 5:4 ('Angelus autem Domini descendebat secundum tempus in piscinam, et movebatur aqua. Et qui prior descendisset ... sanus fiebat a quacumque detinebatur infirmitate') is absent: units pass from 5:3 to 5:5.

notes.latin: Amen , amen dico vobis: qui non intrat per ostium in ovile ovium, sed ascendit aliunde, ille fur est et latro.
notes.english: Amen, amen, I say to you: He that enters not by the door into the sheepfold but climbs up another way, the same is a thief and a robber.
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma in the recorded Latin: 'Amen , amen dico vobis' should read 'Amen, amen dico vobis'. English is unaffected.

notes.latin: Non creditis quia ego in Patre, et Pater in me est? Verba quæ ego loquor vobis, a meipso non loquor. Pater autem in me manens, ipse fecit opera.
notes.english: Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father in me? The words that I speak to you, I speak not of myself. But the Father who abides in me, he does the works.
notes.reason: Recorded 'ipse fecit opera' (perfect) appears to be a typo for the Clementine 'ipse facit opera' (present: 'he does the works'), which the English already renders. Verify against a printed Clementine.

notes.latin: Parthi, et Medi, et Ælamitæ, et qui habitant Mespotamiam, Judæam, et Cappadociam, Pontum, et Asiam,
notes.english: Parthians and Medes and Elamites and inhabitants of Mesopotamia, Judea, and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: "Mespotamiam" should read "Mesopotamiam".

notes.latin: Vir autem quidam nomine Ananias, cum Saphira uxore suo vendidit agrum,
notes.english: But a certain man named Ananias, with Saphira his wife, sold a piece of land,
notes.reason: Latin typo: "cum Saphira uxore suo" should read "cum Saphira uxore sua" (feminine ablative agreeing with uxore).

notes.latin: Philippus autem descendens in civitatem Samariæ, prædicabant illis Christum.
notes.english: And Philip, going down to the city of Samaria, preached Christ to them.
notes.reason: Latin typo: plural "prædicabant" with singular subject Philippus; should read "prædicabat illis Christum".

notes.latin: Et ecclesiæ quidem confirmabantur fide, et abundabunt numero quotidie.
notes.english: And the churches were confirmed in faith and increased in number daily.
notes.reason: Latin typo: future "abundabunt" beside imperfect "confirmabantur"; should read "abundabant numero quotidie" (as the English "increased" renders).

notes.latin: Paulus , servus Jesu Christi, vocatus Apostolus, segregatus in Evangelium Dei,
notes.english: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated to the gospel of God.
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma after the initial word: "Paulus , servus" should read "Paulus, servus Jesu Christi".

notes.latin: Quid enim dicit Scriptura? Credidit Abraham Deo, et reputatam est illi ad justitiam.
notes.english: For what says the scripture? Abraham believed God: and it was reputed to him to justice.
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: "reputatam est illi" should be "reputatum est illi ad justitiam" (neuter, as in 4:22-23).

notes.latin: Ohomo, tu quis es, qui respondeas Deo? numquid dicit figmentum ei qui se finxit: Quid me fecisti sic?
notes.english: O man, who are you that reply against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it: Why have you made me thus?
notes.reason: Glued initial: "Ohomo, tu quis es" should read "O homo, tu quis es".

notes.latin: Fratres , voluntas quidem cordis mei, et obsecratio ad Deum, fit pro illis in salutem.
notes.english: Brothers, the will of my heart, indeed and my prayer to God is for them to salvation.
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma after the initial word: "Fratres , voluntas" should read "Fratres, voluntas quidem cordis mei".

notes.latin: Oaltitudo divitiarum sapientiæ, et scientiæ Dei: quam incomprehensibilia sunt judicia ejus, et investigabiles viæ ejus!
notes.english: O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God! How incomprehensible are his judgments, and how unsearchable his ways!
notes.reason: Glued initial: "Oaltitudo divitiarum" should read "O altitudo divitiarum sapientiæ, et scientiæ Dei".

notes.latin: Et si dixerit auris: Quoniam non sum oculus, non sum de corpore: num ideo est de corpore?
notes.english: And if the ear should say: Because I am not the eye, I am not of the body: Is it therefore not of the body?
notes.reason: LA as recorded reads 'num ideo est de corpore?' without 'non', unlike v.15 and the English ('not of the body'). Apparently a dropped word; expected Latin: 'num ideo non est de corpore?'

notes.latin: Paulus , Apostolus Jesu Christi per voluntatem Dei, et Timotheus frater, ecclesiæ Dei, quæ est Corinthi cum omnibus sanctis, qui sunt in universa Achaia.
notes.english: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother: to the church of God that is at Corinth, with all the saints that are in all Achaia:
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma in the Latin: 'Paulus , Apostolus' should read 'Paulus, Apostolus'.

notes.latin: Ego autem testem Deum invoco in animam meam, quod parcens vobis, non veni ultra Corinthum: non quia dominamur fidei vestæ, sed adjutores sumus gaudii vestri: nam fide statis.
notes.english: But I call God to witness upon my soul that to spare you, I came not any more to Corinth: not because we exercise dominion over your faith: but we are helpers of your joy. For in faith you stand.
notes.reason: Typo in the Latin: 'fidei vestæ' should read 'fidei vestræ'.

notes.latin: Numquid per aliquem eorum, quod misi ad vos, circumveni vos?
notes.english: Did I overreach you by any of them whom I sent to you?
notes.reason: Apparent typo in the Latin: 'eorum, quod misi ad vos' should read 'eorum, quos misi ad vos' (relative agreeing with eorum; EN 'whom I sent' is right).

notes.latin: Paulus , Apostolus non ab hominibus, neque per hominem, sed per Jesum Christum, et Deum Patrem, qui suscitavit eum a mortuis:
notes.english: Paul, an apostle, neither from men nor through a man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead,
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma in the Latin: 'Paulus , Apostolus' should read 'Paulus, Apostolus'.

notes.latin: State , et nolite iterum jugo servitutis contineri.
notes.english: Stand firm, and do not let yourselves be held again under a yoke of slavery.
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma in the Latin: 'State , et' should read 'State, et'.

notes.latin: Fratres , etsi præoccupatus fuerit homo in aliquo delicto, vos, qui spirituales estis, hujusmodi instruite in spiritu lenitatis, considerans teipsum, ne et tu tenteris.
notes.english: Brothers, if anyone is caught in a fault, you who are spiritual should set such a person right in a spirit of gentleness. Each of you should watch yourself, so that you too are not tempted.
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma in the Latin: 'Fratres , etsi' should read 'Fratres, etsi'.

notes.latin: Filii , obedite parentibus vestris in Domino: hoc enim justum est.
notes.english: Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is just.
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma in the Latin: 'Filii , obedite' should read 'Filii, obedite'.

notes.latin: Igitur , si consurrexistis cum Christo: quæ sursum sunt quærite, ubi Christus est in dextera Dei sedens:
notes.english: Therefore if you be risen with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God.
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma in the Latin: 'Igitur , si' should read 'Igitur, si'.

notes.latin: Domini , quod justum est et æquum, servis præstate: scientes quod et vos Dominum habetis in cælo.
notes.english: Masters, do to your servants that which is just and equal: knowing that you also have a master in heaven.
notes.reason: Stray space before the comma in the Latin: 'Domini , quod' should read 'Domini, quod'.

notes.latin: Iis autem, qui ejusmodi sunt, denuntiemus, et obsecramus in Domino Jesu Christo, ut cum silentio operantes, suum panem manducent.
notes.english: We command and urge such people in the Lord Jesus Christ to work quietly and eat their own bread.
notes.reason: "denuntiemus" (subjunctive) appears to be a typo for the Clementine "denuntiamus", indicative parallel to "obsecramus"; the English "We command" already renders the indicative.

notes.latin: et quæ audisti a me per multos testes, hæc commenda fidelibus hominibus, qui idonei erant et alios docere.
notes.english: And the things which you have heard of me by many witnesses, the same commend to faithful men who shall be fit to teach others also.
notes.reason: "qui idonei erant" appears to be a typo for the Clementine "qui idonei erunt" (future); the English "who shall be fit" already renders "erunt".

notes.latin: Si ergo esset super terram, nec esset sacerdos: cum essent qui offerent secundum legem munera,
notes.english: If then he were on earth, he would not be a priest: seeing that there would be others to offer gifts according to the law.
notes.reason: "qui offerent" appears to be a typo for the Clementine "qui offerrent" (imperfect subjunctive after "cum essent"); the English is unaffected.

notes.latin: Quæ autem desursum est sapientia, primum quidem pudica est, deinde pacifica, modesta, suadibilis, bonus consentiens, plena misericordia et fructibus bonis, non judicans, sine simulatione.
notes.english: But the wisdom that is from above, first indeed is chaste, then peaceable, modest, easy to be persuaded, consenting to the good, full of mercy and good fruits, without judging, without dissimulation.
notes.reason: "bonus consentiens" is a typo for the Clementine "bonis consentiens" (dative plural, "consenting to the good"), which the English already renders.

notes.latin: In quo exsultabis, modicum nunc si oportet contristari in variis tentationibus:
notes.english: Wherein you shall greatly rejoice, if now you must be for a little time made sorrowful in various temptations:
notes.reason: "exsultabis" (2nd singular) is a truncation of the Clementine "exsultabitis" (2nd plural), which the English "you shall greatly rejoice" renders.

notes.latin: Similiter et mulieres subditæ sint viris suis: ut etsi qui non credunt verbo, per mulierem conversationem sine verbo lucrifiant:
notes.english: In like manner also, let wives be subject to their husbands: that, if any believe not the word, they may be won without the word, by the conversation of the wives,
notes.reason: "per mulierem conversationem" is a typo for the Clementine "per mulierum conversationem" (genitive plural, "by the conversation of the wives"), as the English has it.

notes.latin: Quod et vos nunc similis formæ salvos fecit baptisma: non carnis depositio sordium, sed conscientiæ bonæ interrogatio in Deum per resurrectionem Jesu Christi.
notes.english: Baptism, corresponding to this, has now saved you also: not the removal of dirt from the flesh, but the appeal of a good conscience toward God, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
notes.reason: "salvos fecit" appears to be a typo for the Clementine "salvos facit" (present, "now saves you"); the English "has now saved" follows the perfect and would need "now saves you also".

notes.latin: libertatem illis promittentes, cum ipsi servi sint corruptionem: a quo enim quis superatus est, hujus et servus est.
notes.english: Promising them liberty, whereas they themselves are the slaves of corruption. For by whom a man is overcome, of the same also he is the slave.
notes.reason: "servi sint corruptionem" is a typo for the Clementine "servi sint corruptionis" (genitive, "slaves of corruption"), as the English has it.
